# `BittrWidget` stills — manually captured, iOS only

**Nothing in here is Maestro output, and nothing here will ever be regenerated by a run.**

Maestro cannot drive the iOS home-screen widget surface or the Xcode preview canvas, so no
flow can produce these files. They are captured by hand on a Mac, following
`shared/docs/widget-capture-runbook.md`, to answer the three questions in
`shared/docs/widget-spec.md` §6 that reading the source cannot settle.

## Why here and not `shared/docs/screenshots/widget/`

BIT-76 originally asked for `shared/docs/screenshots/widget/`. That directory is the
canonical BIT-3 reference set, indexed from the flow YAML by `screenshot_map.py`. Four
stills that no flow declares are reported there as **`orphaned`**, and a cropped tile is a
different pixel size from every full-device flow frame, which also trips the
single-size check — i.e. landing them there turns `--verify` red for a reason that is not a
defect. Measured on a scratch copy of this tree:

| Landing path | `screenshot_map.py --verify shared/docs/screenshots` |
|---|---|
| `shared/docs/screenshots/widget/` | `orphaned=4`, two distinct sizes, `clean=False` |
| `shared/docs/device-checks/widget/` | `orphaned=0` |

`device-checks/` is the directory `screenshot_map.py` already documents (see the comment
above `verify()`) as the home for frames deliberately kept outside the canonical set —
the same reason the per-device `iphone_se/` frames live here.

## Expected contents

| File | State | Appearance |
|---|---|---|
| `widget-light-populated.png` | `€ 94.250` | light |
| `widget-dark-populated.png` | `€ 94.250` | dark |
| `widget-light-na.png` | `€ N/A` | light |
| `widget-dark-na.png` | `€ N/A` | dark |
| `widget-home-light.png` | real home-screen tile (Tier B, optional) | light |
| `widget-home-dark.png` | real home-screen tile (Tier B, optional) | dark |

The capturing simulator model must be recorded in the commit message or on BIT-76: the
rendered point size of the price depends on the tile's point size, which depends on the
device.
